Visual language

Instruments, not stock galaxies.

A small set of motifs repeated with discipline: orbits, hairlines, kicker rules and tone-edged cards. Calm surfaces let the content and the single teal signal do the work.

Motifs

Six devices, used sparingly.

  • Orbit rings

    Use: as a quiet backdrop at 6–12% opacity, or as the mark. Rings turn slowly (25–65 s).

    Avoid: full-opacity rings behind text, or more than one animated element per screen.

  • Section label

    Kicker rule

    Use: a 26px teal rule plus a small uppercase label above a page or hero heading.

    Avoid: using it on every heading. One per page header.

  • The idea

    Label with hairline

    Use: to open a band of content. The hairline runs to the edge of the column.

    Avoid: stacking two labels in one band.

  • ScienceViolet edge

    Tone-edged card

    Use: a 3px left border in a role colour to tag a card’s topic, with the topic written out.

    Avoid: colouring whole card backgrounds.

  • 010203

    Numbered labels

    Use: two-digit teal numbers to order a short sequence of ideas or steps.

    Avoid: numbering lists longer than eight.

  • Tint + borderAmberSky

    Tinted pills

    Use: an 11–13% fill, a 26% border and solid accent text for status and category.

    Avoid: relying on the colour; always write the label.

Generous, ruled and calm.

Photography and imagery

Real instruments, real places.

  • Documentary first. Telescopes, labs, launch sites, data and people at work. Show the thing, not a metaphor for it.
  • Dark and high-contrast. Imagery should sit comfortably on Ink. Avoid pale, washed-out frames.
  • No clichés. No composite galaxies, lens flares, floating astronauts or neon gradients.
  • 16:9 for features, 4:5 for portraits, 1:1 for avatars. Crop to the subject, never stretch.
  • Always credit and caption. Name the agency or photographer, and check each licence: NASA, ESA and ESO terms differ.
  • Always write alt text that says what the image shows and why it is there. Decorative images get an empty alt.

Data and diagrams

Label directly. Never rely on hue.

  • Order series as Teal, Amber, Violet, Sky, Coral, Green. Keep each series’ colour constant across a report.
  • Graphics need 3:1 against their background. On Card, every accent passes.
  • Label lines and bars directly, and vary shape, pattern or dash as well as colour.
  • Give every chart a title, a one-sentence takeaway and a data table or text alternative.

Motion

Slow, optional and quiet.

  • Short transitions

    Colour and border changes take 0.2 s; reveals up to 0.5 s. Nothing bounces.

  • Reduced motion wins

    With prefers-reduced-motion, all animation and smooth scrolling stop.

  • Pause anything long

    Decorative motion lasting over five seconds needs a pause control or must be removable (WCAG 2.2.2).

  • Reveal only with JS

    Scroll-reveal effects apply only when scripting is enabled, so no one is left with hidden content.

One system for science, space and strategy: clear enough to read, distinctive enough to remember.
